component.name: Tessera
component.summary: Share smart card and token drivers with your other apps
Compartilhe os drivers de cartões e tokens com seus outros aplicativos

description.p: Tessera lets sandboxed apps use hardware tokens, smart cards and cloud certificates without installing any driver on the system. It runs the token drivers inside its own sandbox and shares every token with other apps through p11-kit, the standard way for Linux apps to reach PKCS#11 devices.
This is meant for immutable systems such as Fedora Silverblue, Kinoite, Bluefin, Aurora and Bazzite, where installing a vendor's driver package on the host is hard or impossible.

ul.li: Shows the card readers, the inserted tokens and their certificates
OpenSC built in, for Feitian ePass2003, PIV cards and YubiKeys, OpenPGP cards and the many others OpenSC supports

The vendors' drivers are extensions, installed for the token at hand: SafeSign IC (GD Burti), SafeNet Authentication Client and SerproID, each downloaded from its vendor at install time and checked against pinned checksums; others can publish theirs the same way
Says which driver a connected token needs, with its page in the app store and the command that installs it
Opens the drivers' tools, such as SafeSign's Token Administration and the SerproID app

Sets up Firefox, Chromium, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Thunderbird, Evolution, LibreOffice, Papers, Okular, JSignPdf and Master PDF Editor to use the tokens, and shows the command that lets them reach Tessera
Brings the web signers Lacuna Web PKI, Softplan WebSigner (e-SAJ) and Certisign WebSigner, each an extension, to the Flatpak browsers, with the one command each browser needs
Publishes a driver only while it answers, so a driver that hangs cannot hang the apps
Keeps running in the background with an icon in the tray, and can start at login

description.p: Each driver runs in its own p11-kit server inside Tessera. Tessera adds them to the host's p11-kit configuration, and the host's p11-kit server (p11-kit-server.socket, enabled once) serves them to other apps. Sandboxed apps need --filesystem=xdg-run/p11-kit/pkcs11; PJeOffice Pro from FlatPark has it already.
The host needs pcscd with the CCID driver and p11-kit-server, which most distributions ship.
Web signers, and the system's OpenSC out of the way.

ul.li: Lacuna Web PKI, Softplan WebSigner (e-SAJ) and Certisign WebSigner as extensions, for the Flatpak browsers: the new Web signers section shows each browser's one command, and whether it is done.

The system's own OpenSC, which hung the GD Burti token, is switched off for the system's p11-kit from the first start; Tessera's OpenSC serves the same cards. A switch in the Service section turns it back on.
Tessera no longer makes folders for Papers and Okular when they are not installed.
A smaller download: the release no longer carries OpenSC's static library nor pcscd's files.

description.p: Drivers as extensions, OpenSC built in, and more apps.

ul.li: The vendors' drivers (SafeSign IC, SafeNet Authentication Client, SerproID) are now extensions, installed only for the tokens at hand, from the app store or the command line. The window says which one a connected token needs.
OpenSC is built in, for Feitian ePass2003, PIV cards, YubiKeys, OpenPGP cards and the many others it supports. It leaves the GD Burti to SafeSign, and the cards SafeNet serves to SafeNet.
New apps: Thunderbird, Evolution, LibreOffice, JSignPdf, Master PDF Editor and Assinador SERPRO. With several tokens plugged in, JSignPdf's row picks which one it opens.
A driver with no token no longer hides the other drivers' tokens from the apps, which also ends a false warning that the system's p11-kit server was off.
Restart Tessera, in the menu and on an app's row, for an app opened for the first time, or a driver installed, after Tessera started. The refresh button checks the apps at once.
Where the system's p11-kit is too old for signing (Debian 12 and 13, LMDE, Ubuntu 24.04, Linux Mint 22 and the like), a banner says so and links to the documentation.
On the Debian family, which ships no p11-kit-server.socket, the window offers the command that sets up the p11-kit server as a user service.

description.p: Native apps: a new tab sets up the Firefox, Chromium-based browsers, Okular, Papers and PJeOffice Pro installed from the distribution, and leaves alone the ones the system already gives p11-kit (Fedora and its family).

ul.li: Every app shows its own icon, installed or not, and the window keeps its icons on KDE Plasma; the tray icon follows the panel's colors.
SerproID's "approve on your phone" notification shows for every signature on KDE Plasma.
Fewer permissions: no access to the other apps' folders.
Tests of the window and of the detection on Fedora, Debian, Ubuntu, Arch and openSUSE run on every change.

description.p: First release: one p11-kit server per driver (SafeSign IC, SafeNet Authentication Client, SerproID), published through the host p11-kit server; readers, tokens and certificates; set-up for Firefox, Chromium, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Papers and Okular; tray icon and start at login.
